title: Targeting the Rat's Small Bowel: Long-Term Infusion into the Superior Mesenteric Artery
protocol: Cut the larger cannula to about 30 cm in length.
Cut the smaller cannula to about 5 cm in length and insert it 1 cm into the larger cannula.
Fix the two cannulas together with cyanoacrylate glue, avoiding lumen occlusion.
Connect the free extremity of the larger cannula to a Luer stub adapter mounted on a 1 mL syringe filled with saline solution.
Sharpen the free tip of the smaller cannula with scissors.
Check the patency of the cannula by flushing with saline solution.
Perform intramuscular anaesthesia with ketamine/xylazine (100/10 mg/kg).
Shave the fur from the surgical regions: abdomen for SMA cannulation and back of neck for catheter exit.
Clean the surgical regions aseptically using a surgical scrub or solution applied in a circular motion, followed by sterile saline or 70% ethanol, three times.
Test the paw pinch reflex to ensure proper anesthetic depth prior to incision.
Place the animal in a supine position and immobilize the four limbs.
Apply a sterile surgical, water-resistant drape.
Open the abdominal wall with a straight 3 cm incision on the midline of the mesogastric region through all abdominal planes into the peritoneum.
Soak gauzes with saline solution and place them around the laparotomy incision on top of the surgical drape.
Use sutures to keep the surgical incision open.
Identify and expose the small intestine using cotton swabs.
Follow the natural disposition of the small intestine to identify the mesentery.
Extract the mesentery out of the laparotomic cut and lay it downward on the gauzes.
Identify the SMA by feeling the pulsation.
Use cotton swabs to uncover 2-3 proximal branches of the SMA.
Choose a proximal branch of the SMA sufficiently large for surgical maneuvers.
Tie this branch with a 4-0 silk suture, 3-4 cm downstream from its origin.
Place a rigid support under the tied branch of the SMA.
Hold the smaller cannula's extremity using forceps with the dominant hand.
Pull the suture ends with the other hand to strain the vessel and facilitate entry of the catheter.
Hold the tip of the cannula at a 20° angle from the plane of the vessel, in the direction opposite to blood flow.
Lightly press the tip to penetrate the artery wall and insert the cannula without cutting the artery.
Continue inserting the cannula for another 1 cm close to the origin from the SMA.
Fix the cannula to the artery with a surgical knot (4-0 silk).
Verify correct functioning of the cannula by flushing 1 mL of sterile saline solution or by blood sampling.
Place a sterile surgical drape on the incision prior to changing the animal's position.
Create a tunnel from back to abdomen by exerting pressure in the subcutaneous space with a pointed surgical instrument.
Use a sterile surgical drape on the abdomen and back incisions.
Make a 1 cm incision of the posterior region of the neck and accommodate a spherical valve.
Pass the cannula from the laparotomy access to the valve placed in the neck through subcutaneous tissues.
Close the cannula distal extremity with a catheter plug to avoid air inflow.
Replace the small bowel in the abdominal cavity.
Close the abdominal wall and close the skin incisions with a continuous 3-0 silk suture.
Secure the valve to the neck skin with stitches.
Dress the rat with a jacket to protect the button valve after surgery.
Protect the exposed part of the cannula with a steel rod during infusion and secure it to the valve.
Administer NSAID pre-operatively for pain control (5 mg/mL Meloxicam injectable, 1 mg/kg once daily for up to 3 days).
Stabilize the rat in a metabolic cage for the time of infusion (24h) after surgery.
Re-anesthetize the rat with isoflurane inhalation for the time necessary to disassemble the infusion system post-infusion.
House the rat in a normal cage with a 12-hour light/dark cycle and free access to food and water after removing the infusion system.
Stabilize the rat in a metabolic cage.
Connect the distal extremity of the cannula to an elastomeric pump filled with 50 mL of sterile saline solution.
Proceed with infusion for 24 hours.
Administer intramuscular antibiotics (enrofloxacin 10 mg/kg) on the first day.
Pass to oral administration of enrofloxacin (100 mg in 500 mL drinking water).
Dispense analgesic therapy intramuscularly during awakening (ketoprofen 5.0 mg/kg).
Administer paracetamol orally in the following days (200 mg in drinking water).
Monitor body weight measurement and hydration.
Disassemble the animal's external infusion system by removing the pump, jacket, steel rod, and valve after 24 hours of infusion.
Close and cut the cannula as it comes out of the neck, leaving this extremity under the skin of the neck after wound suture if necessary.
House the rat individually in a normal cage with a 12-hour light/dark cycle.
Provide free access to food and water.
